The goal is to identify distinct server-side enforcement sites that control whether a requester may view or read a memo.

APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess governs direct memo reads. APIV1Service.ListMemos enforces visibility filters at query time. APIV1Service.GetMemoByShare provides a share-token bypass path. Connect and gRPC-Gateway both delegate to the same service layer, so they are not separate enforcement sites.

ListMemoAttachments and ListMemoReactions each enforce inline visibility checks. ListMemoRelations and batchConvertMemoRelations apply memoFilter to related memos without requiring parent memo read access. Notification payloads and emails use canViewerAccessMemo to gate memo snippets. RSS feeds restrict visibility to Public only.

Frontend getSitemapXML exposes public memo UIDs and URLs. File server checkAttachmentPermission and attachment API checkAttachmentAccess govern attachment reads. SSEClient.canReceive filters which memo update events a connected client receives. Authorizer and MCP were ruled out as non-enforcement surfaces.

Sitemap XML is marginal because it only exposes memo URLs without content. User stats endpoints filter memos for counts rather than enabling reads. Inline visibility checks in ListMemoAttachments, ListMemoReactions, and ListMemoRelations duplicate logic instead of delegating to checkMemoReadAccess. These surfaces may not qualify as distinct enforcement sites.

Distinct surfaces should be interpreted as transport or protocol boundaries rather than individual API handlers. This yields roughly seven distinct enforcement sites: the unified API surface, share-token bypass, RSS export, file server downloads, SSE live events, email notifications, and in-app notification API.

The final tally is eight distinct enforcement sites. The API surface itself contains multiple independent checks: checkMemoReadAccess for GetMemo and ListMemoComments, ListMemos visibility filtering, and inline visibility guards inside ListMemoAttachments and ListMemoReactions.

I am reconsidering whether inline visibility checks in ListMemoAttachments, ListMemoReactions, and ListMemoRelations should be counted as separate enforcement sites or collapsed into the API surface. The user wants distinct surfaces, so I will likely list each place where the server decides whether a requester can read memo content. value.text:
`GetMemoByShare` in `memo_share_service` uses share tokens rather than `checkMemoReadAccess`.

ListMemoAttachments and ListMemoReactions contain inline read checks. GetMemoByShare still counts as an enforcement site because it grants read access via share tokens. Need to verify that attachment_service.GetAttachment calls checkAttachmentAccess. Distinctness will be judged by API surface, not individual functions.

The first distinct enforcement site is `APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess` in `memo_service.go`, used by `GetMemo`.

`ListMemos` in `memo_service.go` enforces visibility through a CEL filter. `ListMemoComments` in `memo_service_comments.go` uses `checkMemoReadAccess` plus `memoFilter`. RSS endpoints `GetExploreRSS` and `GetUserRSS` in `rss.go` control read access. `checkAttachmentPermission` in `fileserver.go` governs file downloads. `SSEClient.canReceive` in `sse_hub.go` gates SSE events. `checkAttachmentAccess` in `attachment_service.go` governs attachment reads.

`canViewerAccessMemo` in `user_service_notifications.go` and `email.go` restricts notification and email memo access. `getSitemapXML` in `frontend.go` controls sitemap read access. `ListMemoRelations` and `batchConvertMemoRelations` in `memo_relation_service.go` and `memo_service_converter.go` apply `memoFilter` to relation data. These relation and conversion surfaces likely count as distinct enforcement sites for memo-related content.

`user_service_stats` filters memos for statistics. This is borderline because it does not read memo content. API, gRPC, and Connect all share `APIV1Service`. They count as one API surface. The final list will group by truly distinct transport and export channels.

API, RSS, file server, and SSE are distinct surfaces. `checkMemoReadAccess` and `ListMemos` are separate enforcement sites within the API surface. `GetMemoByShare` is distinct because it grants read access solely via an active share token, bypassing visibility checks entirely. `ListMemoRelations` does not verify parent memo read access; it merely filters related memos, yet it still counts as an enforcement site for related memo snippets.

Here are the distinct server-side enforcement sites that gate whether a requester may view/read memo content (or memo-derived content), grouped by transport/surface:

gRPC/Connect/Gateway single-memo read — `APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess` (archived + visibility/auth checks) called from `GetMemo` and parent-memo checks — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway memo list read — `APIV1Service.ListMemos` applies `VisibilityList` and CEL `creator_id`/`visibility` filters before returning memos — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway share-link read — `APIV1Service.GetMemoByShare`/`getActiveMemoShare` grants memo read only for valid, non-expired share tokens (archived memos denied) — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway comment read — `APIV1Service.ListMemoComments` calls `checkMemoReadAccess` on the parent, then filters comment memos via `MemoFilter` visibility CEL — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway relation read — `APIV1Service.ListMemoRelations` filters related-memo snippets via per-user `MemoFilter` visibility CEL — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway embedded relation read — `APIV1Service.batchConvertMemoRelations` applies the same `MemoFilter` when attaching relation snippets to list/get responses — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway attachment metadata read — `APIV1Service.ListMemoAttachments` inline visibility/auth check on the parent memo — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway reaction read — `APIV1Service.ListMemoReactions` inline visibility/auth check on the parent memo — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway attachment binary read — `APIV1Service.checkAttachmentAccess` enforces memo visibility for memo-linked attachments in attachment RPCs — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`

gRPC/Connect/Gateway notification memo snippets — `canViewerAccessMemo` in `convertMemoCommentNotificationPayload`/`convertMemoMentionNotificationPayload` strips memo snippets the viewer cannot read — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`

HTTP file-server attachment read — `FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission` gates memo-linked file bytes by memo visibility, anonymous-instance policy, session auth, or `share_token` query param — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`

HTTP SSE live memo events — `SSEClient.canReceive` in `SSEHub.Broadcast` drops memo update/comment/reaction events the subscriber is not allowed to see by visibility — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

HTTP RSS export — `RSSService.GetExploreRSS`/`GetUserRSS` only query memos with `VisibilityList: []store.Public` — `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`

HTTP sitemap export — `FrontendService.getSitemapXML` only lists public memos (`VisibilityList: []store.Public`) — `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`

Email notification memo content — `canViewerAccessMemo` in email dispatch skips memo/comment snippets the receiver cannot read — `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go`
